screenplay.text:
LOAD SHEDDING

                                     Written by

                                 The Panelwise team






























               Self-written sample screenplay for Panelwise.
               Licence: Apache-2.0, the same as the repository.













               FADE IN:

         1     INT. HIGH SCHOOL - CLASSROOM 4B - EVENING               1

               Rows of wooden desks scratched with initials. A chalkboard
               reads: FINAL MATHS EXAM - 18:00 TO 20:00. Rain against the
               windows.

               MS. MOLEFE (40s), cardigan, red pen tucked behind one ear,
               walks between the desks laying exam papers face down.

               Six learners wait. AYANDA (17), braids, chews her pencil.
               JABU (17), tall, knee bouncing under the desk. FATIMA (16),
               calculator lined up with her ruler.

               PIETER (17), sleepy, hood up. NOMSA (16), praying with her
               eyes closed. And LUCKY (17), at the back, already sweating.

                                     MS. MOLEFE
                         You may turn your papers over. You
                         have two hours. Good luck.

               Paper rustles. Pencils start scratching.

               The lights flicker. Buzz. Then the room goes black.

         2     INT. HIGH SCHOOL - CLASSROOM 4B - CONTINUOUS            2

               Darkness. Rain. A few phone screens glow blue.

                                     LUCKY
                               (whispering)
                         Load shedding. Thank you, Lord.

                                     JABU
                         It's a sign. The exam is cancelled.

                                     MS. MOLEFE (O.S.)
                         Nobody is cancelling anything.
                         Phones face down on the desks.

               A match flares. Ms. Molefe's face appears in the small
               flame. She lights a CANDLE in a saucer.

                                     MS. MOLEFE
                         Every teacher in this country keeps
                         candles in the bottom drawer.
                         Fatima, help me.

                                     FATIMA
                         How many are there, Miss?

                                     MS. MOLEFE
                         Enough.








                                                                       2.


         3     INT. HIGH SCHOOL - CLASSROOM 4B - MOMENTS LATER         3

               Fatima and Ms. Molefe set a candle on every desk. The room
               fills with small trembling lights. Shadows of the learners
               stretch huge across the walls.

               Pieter pulls his hood down and stares at his candle.

                                     PIETER
                         This is actually quite nice.

                                     AYANDA
                         Quiet, Pieter. Some of us are doing
                         question two.

                                     NOMSA
                               (opening her eyes)
                         I can't read the graph. It's too
                         dark.

                                     MS. MOLEFE
                         Bring your desk to the window. The
                         streetlight is still on outside.

                                     NOMSA
                         The streetlight works and the
                         school doesn't?

                                     MS. MOLEFE
                         Welcome to engineering. That's
                         question seven.

               The class laughs. Nomsa drags her desk to the window.

         4     INT. HIGH SCHOOL - CLASSROOM 4B - LATER                 4

               The candles have burned down by half. Wax pools in the
               saucers.

               Lucky stares at a blank page. He looks across at Jabu's
               paper. Jabu covers it with his arm without looking up.

               Ms. Molefe crouches beside Lucky's desk.

                                     MS. MOLEFE
                               (quietly)
                         Which one?

                                     LUCKY
                         All of them, Miss.





                                                            (CONTINUED)






                                                                       3.


               CONTINUED:

                                     MS. MOLEFE
                         Then start with the one you know a
                         little. Not the one you know
                         nothing about.

               Lucky looks at his paper for a long moment. Then he picks up
               his pencil and begins to write.

         5     INT. HIGH SCHOOL - CLASSROOM 4B - NIGHT                 5

               The wall clock reads eight o'clock. Ms. Molefe stands at the
               front.

                                     MS. MOLEFE
                         Pencils down.

               Six pencils go down. The candles are stubs now.

               The lights buzz and flicker on. Everybody squints. Groans.

                                     JABU
                         Now it comes back.

                                     PIETER
                         I liked the candles better.

                                     FATIMA
                               (handing in her paper)
                         Miss, can we write all our exams
                         like this?

                                     MS. MOLEFE
                         Ask the power station.

               Ms. Molefe collects the last paper, from Lucky. There's
               writing on every page. She looks at him. He shrugs, half
               smiling.

               She blows out the last candle.

                                                            FADE OUT.

shots.source:
Rows of wooden desks scratched with initials. A chalkboard reads: FINAL MATHS EXAM - 18:00 TO 20:00. Rain against the windows.

Six learners wait. AYANDA (17), braids, chews her pencil. JABU (17), tall, knee bouncing under the desk. FATIMA (16), calculator lined up with her ruler.
shots.rationale: Establishes the teacher distributing exams and the learners' anxious postures before the test begins.

shots.source:
PIETER (17), sleepy, hood up. NOMSA (16), praying with her eyes closed. And LUCKY (17), at the back, already sweating.
You may turn your papers over. You have two hours. Good luck.
Paper rustles. Pencils start scratching.
shots.rationale: Intimately captures the varied reactions—sleepy, praying, sweating—as the learners start writing.

shots.source: The lights flicker. Buzz. Then the room goes black.
shots.rationale: The sudden blackout is best served by a disorienting extreme close-up with handheld movement to convey the abrupt darkness.

shots.source:
Darkness. Rain. A few phone screens glow blue.
Load shedding. Thank you, Lord.
shots.rationale: Establishes the powerless darkness and the students' whispered reactions to the load shedding.

shots.source:
It's a sign. The exam is cancelled.
Nobody is cancelling anything. Phones face down on the desks.
shots.rationale: Captures Jabu's hopeful declaration against Ms. Molefe's authoritative command to silence phones.

shots.source:
A match flares. Ms. Molefe's face appears in the small flame. She lights a CANDLE in a saucer.
Every teacher in this country keeps candles in the bottom drawer. Fatima, help me.
shots.rationale: Focuses on the match flame and the teachers' shared resolve as they light the candle together.

shots.source:

Enough.
shots.rationale: Frames the exchange about the candle supply, emphasizing the teacher's confidence and the student's question.

Pieter pulls his hood down and stares at his candle.

shots.rationale: Establishes the initial setup of candles and Pieter's reaction in a single, stable frame.

shots.source:

I can't read the graph. It's too dark.
Bring your desk to the window. The streetlight is still on outside.
shots.rationale: Captures the dialogue and Nomsa's struggle with the graph in a clear, centered composition.

shots.source:

Welcome to engineering. That's question seven.
The class laughs. Nomsa drags her desk to the window.
shots.rationale: Frames the teacher's instruction and Nomsa's movement toward the window as a cohesive unit.

The candles have burned down by half. Wax pools in the saucers.
Lucky stares at a blank page. He looks across at Jabu's paper. Jabu covers it with his arm without looking up.
shots.rationale: Establishes the setting and Lucky's distraction by Jabu's paper before intervention.

shots.source:

shots.rationale: Intimate framing captures Ms. Molefe's quiet guidance and Lucky's conflicted reaction.

shots.source: Then start with the one you know a little. Not the one you know nothing about.
shots.rationale: Isolates Lucky's internal decision before he commits to writing.

shots.source: Lucky looks at his paper for a long moment. Then he picks up his pencil and begins to write.
shots.rationale: Shows the physical act of beginning to write, marking the transition from hesitation to action.

Six pencils go down. The candles are stubs now.
shots.rationale: Establishes Ms. Molefe's authority as she gives the initial command.

shots.rationale: Captures the boys' contrasting reactions to the exam ending.
